headline: A full design-system Tabs is where class-name length turns into CPU: `bamboo` and `panda` do no styling work and still spend three quarters of their JS window in react-dom writing the class attribute.

microbench.why: `vanilla` (0.838 ms/1k) and `next-yak-css-9.7` (0.858) render the tab group as plain elements with one class each, and `stylex-layers` (0.871) with a handful of hashed atomic classes. The libraries that name classes after their declarations pay for it in react-dom: `bamboo` at 2.20 ms/1k and `panda` at 2.53 have library slices of 0.012 and 0.000 ms, and 74.0 and 92.2 ms of their JS windows are react-dom escaping selector text out of the class attribute. `emotion` (5.82) and `styled-components` (3.92) lose for the opposite reason, re-hashing the whole state matrix per tab.

autocannon.why: `vanilla` serves 720 req/s and `next-yak-css-9.7` 672 on 2.37-2.69 kB responses. Every atomic and utility lane writes a kilobyte-scale class attribute per tab and lands at 190-250 req/s regardless of how little styling code runs, `bamboo` 222 and `panda` 193 against `tailwind-merge`'s 190. The hashing lanes fall further, `emotion` to 135, because they add per-request work on top of the bytes.

attribution.why: `next-yak-css-9.7` compiles the whole state matrix into numbered classes and keeps a 0.108 ms library slice, so its 1.39 ms is react-dom and little else. `bamboo` reports 0.012 ms of library time and still costs 3.08 ms, with 2.75 of it React; `panda` reports zero and costs 3.66 ms with 3.36 React. That is the case's point: their styling is genuinely free and their naming is not. next-yak's styled API sits at 2.21 ms with a 0.898 ms library slice because a styled component wrapping another component keeps a runtime wrapper the fold cannot remove.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

hydrate.why: Every lane with a static sheet hydrates in 48.1-57.0 ms of pure JS, zero style and zero layout inside the span. `goober` (199 ms) and `styled-components` (206 ms) inject during hydration and their spans carry 2.13 and 2.23 ms of style recalculation plus a 3.5-3.7 ms layout, and Chrome presents 18 paints instead of 1 while the sheet arrives in pieces.

inp.why: Switching tabs re-renders one group, and it costs under 1.1 ms of span JS in every lane whose classes are already decided, a 6.7-8.1 ms cluster whose internal order is inside the measurement noise. `emotion` needs 28.1 ms, re-serializing and re-hashing the state matrix for the tab that changed (0.938 ms of `@emotion/hash` in the span), and `goober` 15.2 ms.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

mount.why: Cold mount is the sheet parse plus first paint, 95.1-115 ms for everything that ships a file. `emotion` (232 ms), `styled-components` (209) and `goober` (204) build the sheet first and their mount spans show 1.61-1.64 ms of recalculation and 18 presented frames. `panda` mounts at 100 ms, inside the floor cluster, because its `css()` calls are hoisted to module scope here and resolve once.

renderTiming.why: Counts tie at one recalculation for every lane, but the paint counts do not: `emotion`, `goober` and `styled-components` present 18 frames and run two layout passes where every extracted lane runs one and presents one. That is injection during hydration made visible, and it costs them 1.61-1.64 ms of recalculation against the 0.869-1.04 ms of every lane that loads a finished sheet.

payload.why: Identical CSS costs 2.37 kB gzipped through the css-prop fold and 16.1 kB through `panda`, because atomic naming writes each declaration into the sheet and again into every element that uses it: `panda` carries 10.1 kB of markup and `bamboo` 8.82 against `vanilla`'s 1.62. The utility lanes are worse still, `tailwind-merge` 21.0 kB and `cnfast` 22.0, since their sheet is scanned rather than derived from what the page uses.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

nsweep.why: At 4,000 tab groups the flat lanes hold their line, `vanilla` 30.7 ms and `stylex` 30.9, and `next-yak-css-9.7` 33.5. next-yak's styled API reaches 64.3 ms because the `FullWidthTabs` wrapper keeps one runtime component per group that the fold cannot erase. `panda` (119 ms), `styled-components` (163) and `emotion` (195) scale their per-instance work with n.

crossCase: The Example `multifile-composition` shown below is this case with the styled primitives moved into an imported module and nothing else changed, so the gap between the two is the price of the module boundary. It is small: `next-yak-css-9.7` goes from 0.858 to 0.899 ms/1k and from 33.5 to 36.0 ms at n=4,000, and ships byte-identical 2.37 kB payloads in both. Read the boundary off the sweep rather than the microbench here, since `next-yak-9.7`'s microbench sample in this case carries a 42% spread.
